_doc: Form/setting recipes. Each record of a row gets one recipe code from its plan. min_age = youngest age bracket where the recipe makes sense. Twists are added when a row needs more variants than eligible recipes.

R1.text: Third-person narrative in an urban Indian setting (city flat, colony, market, school, office).

R2.text: Dialogue-heavy family or home scene (mostly spoken lines, little narration), any setting.

R3.text: First-person reflective account by the protagonist, looking back a little (for 7-12 keep it simple and short).

R4.text: A note written by an adult who watched: caregiver, teacher, counsellor, coach or supervisor (their observations, plus what they did next).

R5.text: A diary or journal entry by the protagonist, written the same day, informal.

R6.text: A chat or text-message exchange (short lines), with a few narrator words only if needed; emojis may appear as real people use them.

R7.text: Third-person narrative in a rural or small-town Indian setting (village, farm, kasba, local bus, temple fair, small shop).

R8.text: Third-person narrative set outside India (any country), ordinary everyday detail.

R9.text: Scene set inside an institution: school, hostel, clinic waiting room, workplace, sports club, community centre.

R10.text: A letter or an email written by the protagonist to someone, in a natural voice.

R11.text: An interview-style or spoken monologue: the protagonist tells the story aloud to a friend, podcast host or interviewer.

R12.text: An observer's account: a neighbour, sibling, classmate or colleague describes what they saw, without knowing the protagonist's inner state for sure.

R13.text: Before / during / after across a few days or weeks, in three short beats showing change over time.

R14.text: An elder (grandparent, uncle, senior colleague) tells the story to a younger person as a memory or example, in their voice.

R15.text: Third-person narrative with a complication or constraint added (time pressure, little money, a noisy place, a missing person, bad weather), still faithful to the row.

twists.T1: Set it in a different season or festival period than a typical scene.
twists.T2: Include a sibling, cousin or close friend as a secondary character who reacts.
twists.T3: Use a different time of day (early morning, late night, afternoon lull) and let it matter.
twists.T4: Give the protagonist a different family or work background (single parent, joint family, migrant, first-generation student, shift worker).
twists.T5: Make a small object (phone, bag, tiffin, bicycle, notebook) important in the scene.
twists.T6: Let the scene happen while travelling or moving between places.
